name: Assembly101
summary: People disassemble and reassemble 101 types of toy vehicles without fixed step-by-step instructions. Synchronized egocentric and external views capture natural changes in action order, assembly mistakes, and rework.
duration: Mean sequence duration: 7.1 minutes, with a standard deviation of 3.4 minutes; minimum and maximum durations are unverified. Mean fine-grained action duration: 1.7 seconds; mean coarse-grained action duration: 16.5 seconds.
duration_short: Mean 7.1 min (SD 3.4 min); min-max unverified
total: 362 independent sequences; 4,321 camera-view videos totaling 513 hours across views.
modalities: Synchronized video from 8 fixed RGB cameras and 4 head-mounted grayscale cameras; camera calibration and 3D hand poses.
access: Links only, as checked on 2026-10-24: the official site announced migration to Hugging Face in May 2026; the download repository still contained older Google Drive tools. Account requirements and complete video downloads were not verified.
license: Data and annotations: CC BY-NC 4.0, stated on the official site and annotation README. Open access does not authorize commercial redistribution.
family: Assembly101
caveats: The 7.1-minute mean and 3.4-minute standard deviation are not a minimum-to-maximum range. Count synchronized views once per independent execution and split by execution to avoid leakage. Mistake annotations cover 328 assembly sequences, not all 4,321 view videos. Some mistakes explicitly have no correction; observed rework does not establish an optimal repair policy. Recovery-pair coverage was not verified. README examples contain possible timestamp anomalies, but the full CSV files were not audited and cannot be assumed to share those anomalies. The tasks use toys.

name: IndustReal
summary: Participants assemble, maintain, and replace parts of a 3D-printed construction toy car in a controlled industrial-style setting. Egocentric recordings capture correct steps, omitted steps, and incorrect assembly with part-state and completion annotations.
duration: Minimum and maximum video durations are unverified. The mean is approximately 4.14 minutes, calculated from the reported 5.8 hours divided by 84 videos.
duration_short: Derived mean ~4.14 min (5.8 h / 84 videos); min-max unverified
total: 84 videos totaling 5.8 hours; 27 participants. The project page rounds the duration to approximately 6 hours.
tasks: Correct and incorrect step completion recognition
modalities: HoloLens 2 egocentric RGB, grayscale stereo, depth, hand and head poses, and gaze; 3D part geometry.
access: Links only, as checked on 2026-10-24: the official repository links a 4TU data record and records release on 2023-11-01. The 4TU page request timed out; downloads were not tested.
license: The code repository has an Apache-2.0 license and its README broadly describes IndustReal as Apache-2.0. The 4TU data license was not verified, so that statement does not establish the final license for video and 3D assets.
family: IndustReal
caveats: The mean is derived from a dataset total and does not show that every video meets a long-duration threshold. The 38 incorrect completions are events, not 38 error classes; 35 videos contain omissions or incorrect completions, and 48 execution orders are reported. Natural and deliberately induced errors coexist, with their proportions unverified. Several execution errors appear only in validation/test, so preserve the original split. The dataset covers one toy product family and does not provide a validated optimal correction policy.

name: ENIGMA-51
summary: Participants repair circuit boards in a simulated industrial laboratory while following audio and augmented-reality guidance. Egocentric videos show interactions with oscilloscopes, power supplies, electric screwdrivers, and other repair tools across two procedures.
duration: Minimum and maximum video durations are unverified. The derived mean is approximately 25.9 minutes, using the official rounded total of 22 hours divided by 51 videos.

total: 51 egocentric videos totaling 22 hours; 19 participants and 2 repair procedures.

access: Links only, as checked on 2026-10-24: the official page lists separate video, annotation, and textual-procedure download entries. File retrieval was not tested.

name: IMPACT
summary: Participants assemble and disassemble a commercial angle grinder using professional tools in a controlled setting. Five synchronized views record multiple valid execution orders, assembly states, anomalies, and recovery actions.
duration: Minimum and maximum trial durations are unverified. The derived mean is approximately 4.3 minutes, using approximately 8 hours of independent execution time divided by 112 trials.
duration_short: Derived mean ~4.3 min (~8 independent h / 112 trials); min-max unverified
total: 112 trials by 13 participants; approximately 8 independent hours and 39.5 accumulated hours across 5 views.
modalities: 1 egocentric and 4 external RGB views; the release manifest lists depth for the 4 external views, egocentric audio and gaze, and features.
access: Links only, as checked on 2026-10-24: the official repository provides version 1.1 Google Drive and Hugging Face links, samples, and checksum manifests. Downloads and checksum validation were not run.
license: Data assets and author documentation: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, verified in LICENSE-DATA. Code, scripts, and configuration: Apache-2.0. Third-party or separately licensed files retain their own terms.
family: IMPACT

The manifest does not establish egocentric depth availability. Prediction of observed future actions is not an optimal decision policy. Version 1.1 reflects a July 2026 revision. name: IndEgo
summary: Workers perform industrial assembly, disassembly, inspection, repair, woodworking, and logistics tasks, including two-person collaboration. The collection mixes complete task recordings with tool demonstrations and short actions, using egocentric and external views where available.
duration: Mixed units: individual actions last a few seconds to less than 1 minute, while complete tasks reach up to 68 minutes. The reported overall mean is 205 seconds (3.42 minutes); a unified minimum-to-maximum range is not reported.
duration_short: Overall mean 205 s; actions <1 min; complete tasks up to 68 min; unified range unreported
total: 3,460 egocentric recordings totaling 197.1 hours and 1,092 external-view recordings totaling 96.8 hours; these are not additive independent task hours.
modalities: Egocentric and external video, narrated audio, gaze, motion, hand poses, and semi-dense point clouds; external views are not available for every subset.
access: Open file listing, as checked on 2026-10-24: the institutional Hugging Face repository exposes a data card and file entries. Downloads were not tested. Completion of the announced directory reorganization was not verified, and a viewer type-conversion error did not establish that raw files were unavailable.
license: The institutional data card states CC BY 4.0; additional package-specific terms were not checked.
family: IndEgo
caveats: The 68-minute figure is a maximum for complete tasks, not the duration of all videos. Some QA and collaboration benchmarks use 1-minute slices. Short actions, tool demonstrations, complete tasks, and overlapping views must be distinguished; fix the version and manifest before evaluating long sequences. Error timestamp coverage, recovery pairing, and the balance of spontaneous versus induced errors were not verified. QA does not itself establish an online next-step decision task.

duration: The original paper reports 997-7,262 frames per video; at 30 fps, this corresponds to approximately 33.23-242.07 seconds. The paper reports a mean of 98.40 seconds, retained as stated.

license: The data license was not verified; paper or code licensing must not be substituted for a data license.

summary: People assemble four types of furniture across five environments. Synchronized camera views capture part handling and assembly actions with pose, part-segmentation, and tracking annotations.

total: 371 assembly samples with 3 RGB views per sample; approximately 35.27 accumulated video hours and 48 participants.

name: IPAD
summary: Real and synthetic videos depict periodic production processes for 16 types of industrial equipment. The collection supports analysis of process cycles and temporal anomalies in machine operation.
duration: Per-video minimum, maximum, and mean durations are unverified. Equipment operating cycles last 5-30 seconds; these are cycle lengths, not video durations.

total: More than 6 hours of real and synthetic video covering 16 equipment types.
modalities: Real and synthetic industrial process video.
access: Links only, as checked on 2026-10-24: the original paper provides a project link. Download availability was not verified.
license: The data license was not verified; paper or code licensing must not be substituted for a data license.

Operator step, intent, next-action decision, and recovery supervision are not provided by the verified description.

summary: Participants follow instructions to assemble a metal toy motorcycle with small parts and hand tools. Egocentric video records screw, nut, and wrench interactions alongside depth and gaze for fine-grained action and active-object analysis.
duration: Complete video duration range: 9.23-35.45 minutes. The paper text reports a mean of 21.14 minutes, while its comparison table reports 20.79 minutes; both are retained as decimal-minute values.
duration_short: Range 9.23-35.45 min; conflicting means: text 21.14 min, table 20.79 min

Predicting the next interaction object does not identify an optimal assembly step. Align original and multimodal versions before combining them.

name: CaptainCook4D
summary: Head-mounted recordings capture complete recipe executions in home kitchens, including deliberate deviations and unintentional mistakes. Step and fine-grained action annotations, seven error categories, and recipe dependency graphs support procedural understanding and error analysis.
duration: Recording minimum and maximum are unknown; the derived mean is approximately 14.766 minutes (94.5 hours x 60 / 384 recordings). This is the recording mean, not the mean step-clip duration.
duration_short: Recordings: derived mean ~14.766 min; min/max unknown
total: 384 recordings totaling 94.5 hours; 24 recipes, 8 participants, and 10 kitchens. Approximately 5.3K step and 10K action annotations; their cumulative annotated duration is unknown. Synchronized modalities do not add independent recording hours.
modalities: Head-mounted GoPro Hero11 and HoloLens2 RGB, depth, audio, IMU, and head/hand tracking.
access: As of 2026-10-24: Open; the official site lists a downloader and annotation repository. Media and annotation packages were not downloaded or tested.
license: The official data section explicitly states Apache License 2.0 for the data; this is not inferred from the code license.
family: Independent CaptainCook4D collection; synchronized sensor streams represent the same executions.
caveats: The duration mean is derived from published collection totals. Recipe selection based on preparation times of at most 30 minutes does not establish a recording maximum; complete-process coverage needs sample-level screening. Errors combine staged deviations and unintended mistakes. Split by recipe, operator, and kitchen as appropriate; dependency graphs permit alternative valid orders. Counterfactual correction outcomes are not established by the native benchmark.

name: EPIC-Tent
summary: Participants assemble a tent outdoors while synchronized egocentric cameras and eye tracking record the process. Action, error, uncertainty, and gaze annotations support analysis of assembly progress, hesitation, and recovery.
duration: 2019 paper, 24-participant version: full recordings average 13.6 minutes, with minimum and maximum unknown; task-completion segments range from 4.3 to 24.1 minutes and average 12.1 minutes. For the 2020 repository version with 29 participants, per-video minimum, maximum, and mean are unknown; the older mean does not transfer to this version.
duration_short: 2019: recording mean 13.6 min; task segments 4.3-24.1 min; 2020 video stats unknown
total: 2019 paper version: 24 participants and approximately 5.4 hours. Bristol release dated 2020-08-10: 29 participants, over 7 hours, and 166.8 GiB. GoPro, SMI, and gaze-overlay renderings are synchronized views or representations, not two or three times as many independent session hours.
modalities: Synchronized egocentric GoPro and SMI video with eye tracking; a third-person overview is not guaranteed.
access: As of 2026-10-24: Open; hosted Bristol files and the official annotation repository were visible. Media were not downloaded.
license: Hosted data use the Non-Commercial Government Licence for public sector information, not CC BY. The annotation repository code license was not verified.
family: Independent EPIC-Tent collection with distinct 2019 paper and 2020 hosted versions.
caveats: The 2020 figures of 29 participants and over 7 hours remain valid; do not combine them with the 2019 duration statistics. The 4.3-24.1-minute range describes task-completion segments, not full recordings. Omission annotations lack usable end times; order-error intervals describe the action being performed. Treating all error types as ordinary temporal intervals would misrepresent their semantics.

name: HoloAssist
summary: A performer manipulates physical objects while a remote instructor provides spoken guidance. Multimodal recordings include hierarchical actions, dialogue, and mistake/correction attributes for studying collaborative assistance.
duration: Full task-session minimum and maximum are unknown. The derived mean is approximately 4.484 minutes using the internally matched 2023 paper figures of 166 hours and 2,221 sessions; fine-grained action durations in seconds do not describe entire sessions.
duration_short: Sessions: derived mean ~4.484 min (2023 paper); min/max unknown
total: 2023 paper: 166 hours across 2,221 sessions. Official site: 169 hours and 350 instructor-performer pairs. These are separate reporting bases: do not divide 169 hours by 2,221 or treat participant pairs as sessions. Seven synchronized streams do not add independent hours.
modalities: HoloLens egocentric RGB, depth, audio, gaze, hand/head poses, IMU, camera calibration, and dialogue transcripts.
access: As of 2026-10-24: Open; the official site lists video, sensor, label, and split downloads. Downloads and media availability were not tested.
license: The official site identifies the data license as CDLAv2 (Community Data License Agreement v2). The exact license text and separate code license were not checked.
family: Independent HoloAssist collection; upstream source for EgoVoice, whose selected subset is smaller than the full collection.
caveats: The reason for the paper/site difference of 166 versus 169 hours is unknown; neither total should silently replace the other. EgoVoice uses a 124.8-hour upstream subset, not all HoloAssist footage. Native mistake detection uses history within the current coarse step; intervention-type prediction uses 1/3/5-second windows, and hand prediction uses 3 seconds of history. These tasks do not establish full-session memory or closed-loop assistance effectiveness. Recorded mistakes are real within controlled collaboration tasks.

name: Ego-Exo4D
summary: Synchronized first- and third-person recordings capture skilled activities such as cooking, repair, sports, and music. Key steps, action descriptions, expert commentary, proficiency, and pose annotations support multiview skill understanding.
duration: V2 take/full-session minimum, maximum, and mean are unknown. task_start_sec and task_end_sec mark task boundaries within a take; cropped keystep benchmark clips are a separate sample unit.
duration_short: V2 full takes/sessions: min/max/mean unknown; keystep clips are separate
total: V2: 5,035 takes, 1,286.30 hours summed across all camera views, and 221.26 hours of egocentric footage. Deduplicated synchronized-session hours were not separately verified. Neither 1,286.30 / 5,035 nor an assumed one-to-one equal-length ego stream per take establishes a session mean.
modalities: Aria egocentric and multiple GoPro third-person views, audio, gaze, trajectories, 3D point clouds, and body/hand poses.
access: As of 2026-10-24: Gated; official instructions require accepting the data agreement and obtaining credentials. Full takes and keystep clips have separate downloads; downloading was not tested.
license: A dedicated Ego-Exo4D data agreement governs use and redistribution. Ego4D code licenses do not establish the media license.
family: Independent Ego-Exo4D collection, not a subset of Ego4D; multiple synchronized views share a take.
caveats: The V2 totals are retained with distinct all-view and ego units, following the 2024-03-25 and 2024-09-01 changelog entries. Keystep clips do not establish full-take lengths; screen long procedures using take task boundaries. Annotation coverage varies by take. Sports and music may require separate strata, and views of the same take must stay in one split. Expert quality feedback is not verified as uniform temporal error ground truth.

name: Ego4D Goal-Step
summary: Goal annotations cover diverse Ego4D activities, while a smaller cooking-focused subset adds hierarchical steps and substeps. Temporal boundaries and goal descriptions support offline localization and online procedural recognition.
duration: Original paper Table 1: the full goal-label set has a reported mean video duration of approximately 23 minutes; the 851-video step/substep subset averages approximately 26 minutes. Minimum and maximum are unknown for both. The mean annotated segment duration of 32.5 seconds is not a whole-video mean.
duration_short: Video means: goal set ~23 min; step subset ~26 min; min/max unknown
total: Goal-label set: 7,353 videos, 2,807 video hours, and 319 goal classes. Nested step subset: 851 videos, 368 video hours, 47,721 step/substep segments, 86 goals, and 514 step classes. The 430 annotated-segment hours can overlap hierarchically and are not 430 independent video hours; subsets must not be added.
modalities: Egocentric video with hierarchical textual goals, steps, substeps, and temporal annotations.
access: As of 2026-10-24: Underlying video is gated through Ego4D credentials; official instructions provide the goalstep CLI benchmark filter. The annotation repository is public, and the paper describes CLI annotation delivery. Downloading was not tested.
license: Underlying video follows the Ego4D agreement. Annotation terms are inconsistent: the repository README states MIT; the paper datasheet says annotations need no license/restrictions in one place, while Section C.6 describes distribution under the standard Ego4D agreement. The applicable terms must be checked for each file or release package.
family: Annotations on existing Ego4D footage, not newly recorded video; overlaps with other Ego4D-derived datasets are possible.
caveats: Use 368 video hours for the step subset and 430 cumulative annotated-segment hours, not 430 independent video hours. A downstream 15-30-minute sampling window is not a full-dataset range. Ego4D v2.1 regrouped previously split continuous footage involving 210 original videos; preserve group-to-video_uid mappings for splits. is_relevant marks relevance to a parent goal and is_continued marks continuation, neither an error label. ProVideLLM uses this dataset for online step detection and transfer; its next-step experiments on COIN and Assembly101 must not be attributed to Goal-Step.

name: HD-EPIC
summary: Unscripted cooking recordings span days and kitchens, capturing detailed object interactions and recipe preparation. Dense action, audio, gaze, object, and 3D annotations connect individual observations to recipes and spatial context.
duration: Full videos have a reported mean of 15.9 minutes and standard deviation of 14.5 minutes; minimum and maximum are unknown. Recording starts when a participant enters the kitchen and ends on leaving, so one video is not necessarily one complete recipe.
duration_short: Full videos: mean 15.9 min, SD 14.5 min; min/max unknown
total: 156 videos totaling 41.3 hours in the paper; the official-site figure of 41 hours is rounded. Collection covers 9 kitchens and 69 recipes, with 59.4K actions, 50.9K audio events, 19.9K object tracks, and 26.6K VQA questions. modalities: Project Aria egocentric video, audio, gaze, 3D information, and scene digital twins; object tracks and hand masks.
access: As of 2026-10-24: Open; the official Bristol record lists data files totaling 2.3 TiB. Files were not downloaded or checked.
license: The Bristol data record explicitly states CC BY 4.0. This does not establish licenses for all related datasets or code.
family: Independent HD-EPIC collection, distinct from EPIC-KITCHENS-100 and EPIC Fields; upstream footage for Minerva-Ego.
caveats: The audit refines the rounded 41-hour figure to 41.3 hours and adds the video mean. Recipe elapsed times and participant totals of 3.5-7.2 hours must not be presented as individual-video ranges. The density of 263 annotations per minute combines annotation types rather than counting 263 steps. High annotation density does not establish error ground truth or native next-action decision supervision.

name: 50Salads
summary: Participants prepare salads in a fixed setting while RGB-D video and object-mounted accelerometers record hand, tool, and ingredient interactions. Multilevel activity intervals include preparation, core, and post-action phases for temporal activity analysis.
duration: Full-sequence minimum, maximum, and exact mean remain unknown. The often-quoted approximately 5-10-minute range was not confirmed from the primary-source material obtained. The original abstract states over 4.5 hours for 50 sequences, implying only a mean greater than 5.4 minutes, not a typical duration.
duration_short: Full sequences: mean >5.4 min (derived lower bound); exact mean/min/max unknown
total: 50 sequences from 25 participants preparing two salads each. The UbiComp 2013 abstract states over 4.5 hours of synchronized accelerometer and RGB-D data; the official dataset description more broadly says over 4 hours. These compatible lower bounds are not exact totals. Synchronized sensors do not add independent hours; cumulative annotation duration is unknown.
modalities: Third-person RGB-D video, object-mounted accelerometers, and multilevel temporal activity labels.
access: As of 2026-10-24: Open; the Dundee record provides a README and the original data-site entry point. Availability of files on the older site was not tested.
license: The Dundee dataset record states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; commercial use and unrestricted redistribution are not implied.
family: Independent 50Salads collection with synchronized video and object-sensor streams.
caveats: The canonical 2026-10-31 follow-up accepts the original abstract's >4.5-hour lower bound, correcting an earlier overly conservative audit that retained only >4 hours. The complete original paper was not obtained, so the 5-10-minute range is unconfirmed rather than proven absent. Secondary reports of 6.4-minute means or 5.3-hour totals were not adopted. A single task domain and limited scene variation constrain generalization; dedicated failure labels were not established.

name: Breakfast Actions
year: CVPR 2014; official download notes documented in 2026
summary: Multicamera recordings show participants preparing breakfast in different kitchens. Activity classes and coarse and fine action segments provide a controlled setting for recognition and temporal segmentation.
duration: CVPR 2014 full single-view videos have a derived mean of approximately 2.323 minutes (139.37 seconds), using approximately 77 hours and 1,989 videos summed across the paper's ten class counts. duration_short: Video means, derived: 2014 ~2.323 min; 2016 annotated set ~2.338 min; min/max unknown
total: CVPR 2014: approximately 77 hours and 1,989 videos. The 2016 extended manuscript reports 1,712 action-annotated videos and 66.7 hours. Keep these bases separate. Collection includes 52 participants, 18 kitchens, 10 activities, 48 action units, and 3-5 cameras per location; totals include multiple views and the paper also mentions mirroring. Deduplicated session hours are unknown.
modalities: Multiview third-person RGB, coarse/fine temporal labels, and Fisher-vector features.
access: As of 2026-10-24: Open links to data and annotation mirrors are listed, but the official site says the raw-video mirror is incomplete and reports a Google Drive quota issue dated 2026-10-11. Complete media availability was not verified and downloads were not tested.
license: An explicit data license was not verified on the official site. Mirror metadata and tool-code licenses do not replace original authorization.
family: Independent Breakfast collection; synchronized camera views must not be counted as separate executions.
caveats: The canonical follow-up adds derived means from matched paper versions; do not cross-divide or add their totals. The original 100k figure counts sampled codebook-training features, while 11,267 counts coarse action instances, including approximately 3,600 silence instances; neither counts full videos. The 2016 table's 26.0-second mean is for action segments. Media were not measured file by file. Low resolution, controlled scenes, multiview duplication, and incomplete mirrors limit use; dedicated failure labels were not established.

name: COIN
summary: YouTube instructional videos cover everyday procedures across 12 domains and 180 tasks. A domain-task-step hierarchy and manually labeled step intervals support broad instructional-video understanding.
duration: Full source-video durations range from 4.411667 to 1,236.250167 seconds (approximately 0.0735-20.6042 minutes), with a mean of 142.341911 seconds (approximately 2.372365 minutes), computed from duration fields in 11,827 official COIN.json records. Annotated steps range from 1 to 304 seconds and average 14.908616 seconds.
duration_short: Source videos: min-max 4.411667-1,236.250167 s; mean 142.341911 s
total: Official JSON: 11,827 video durations sum to 1,683,477.776057 seconds (approximately 467.632716 hours). The 46,354 step intervals sum to 691,074 seconds (approximately 191.965 hours), without merging overlaps. The website separately reports 476 hours and a 2.36-minute mean. These conflicting statistics remain distinct.
tasks: Derived next-step and long-horizon step prediction
modalities: Web video, potentially including source audio, with task/step categories and temporal intervals.
access: As of 2026-10-24: Hosted media copies require an institutional representative to sign an agreement and request access by email. Video URLs and annotation JSON are public for separate YouTube retrieval; registration/login is also listed. No request or media-download test was performed.
license: The official annotation README restricts its codes and files to research while allowing sharing and modification. Hosted video copies require a separate license agreement; a uniform CC BY-NC license was not established.
family: COIN instructional-video collection; source YouTube IDs should be used to check overlap with other web-video datasets.
caveats: The audit read and computed official metadata, without downloading media or running ffprobe. The reason for the website's 476 hours versus the JSON's approximately 467.633 hours is unknown; 476 x 60 / 11,827 is approximately 2.4148 minutes, also unlike the reported 2.36-minute mean. Edited tutorials may omit transitions and are not continuous full-task sessions. ProVideLLM supplies derived step-prediction protocols, not closed-loop decision evaluation; dedicated procedural-error labels were not verified.

license: A dedicated Ego4D data agreement governs video access and use. Tool-repository licenses do not replace it.

name: EgoPlan / EgoPlan-IT / EgoPlan-Bench
summary: Goal-conditioned questions ask which action should come next given an egocentric observation and action history. The first-generation benchmark combines EPIC-KITCHENS and Ego4D examples, while EgoPlan-IT supplies instruction-tuning questions from EPIC-KITCHENS.
duration: Minimum, maximum, and mean duration of each question's history video are unknown, and full source-session ranges were not verified. History up to the current action and the current observation are the relevant context units; full EPIC-KITCHENS or Ego4D recording lengths must not be substituted.
duration_short: Per-question history and source-session durations unknown
total: 4,939 evaluation multiple-choice questions across 419 scenarios. Goal counts conflict within the sources: 3,296 in the text versus 3,269 in arXiv v3 Table 2. EgoPlan-IT has 50K automatically constructed planning questions; 50K auxiliary action-recognition instructions reuse observations, and 164K external general instructions are separate. Deduplicated source-video hours and cumulative question-history hours are unknown.
modalities: Video/image observations, textual goals, action histories, and multiple-choice answers.
access: As of 2026-10-24: Open annotation entry points for Val/Test questions and IT data are listed in the official repository; the paper states that Test answer keys are withheld. Underlying EPIC-KITCHENS and Ego4D video must be obtained separately, with credentials required for Ego4D. Downloads were not tested.
license: The paper states CC BY-NC 4.0 for EgoPlan-Val/Test/IT and BSD 3-Clause for code and models. Underlying media retain their respective EPIC-KITCHENS and Ego4D terms.
family: First-generation annotations derived from EPIC-KITCHENS and Ego4D; EgoPlan-IT uses EPIC-KITCHENS only. No new recording hours are established.
caveats: Keep the conflicting 3,296/3,269 goal counts explicit. QA and instruction counts are not independent videos and cannot establish duration. The 2026 journal publication does not imply new footage. Split by source video ID to prevent overlap across derivatives. This is offline next-action selection, not evidence of counterfactually optimal planning, closed-loop execution, or real procedural-error labels.

summary: CALVIN records simulated robot play with drawers, sliding doors, switches, lights, and objects across four environment layouts. Scene states, actions, and partially language-labeled intervals support language-conditioned control and evaluation of sequential task chains.

duration_short: Training windows: 1-2 s; continuous play-session and task-chain durations unknown
total: 24 hours of original play data, approximately 6 hours per environment across 4 environments. Overlapping training windows do not add recording hours.
modalities: Simulated RGB, robot and scene states, actions, episode frame data, and language-labeled intervals; exact modality coverage depends on the data version.
access: As of 2026-10-24: Open: the official dataset README links D, ABC, ABCD, and debug packages with checksums; frame observations can be converted into offline videos. Dataset downloads and playback were not tested.
license: Repository MIT applies explicitly to software. A separate data license was not verified, so redistribution rights for all recordings are unconfirmed.

caveats: Continuous play sequences and second-scale training windows are different units; compositional task-chain evaluation does not make each training sample a long video. Paper section III-B.1 reports 24 hours and 1-2-second relabeled windows, while the dataset README reports about 6 hours per environment. Play is not necessarily a successful procedure, and language labels cover only some intervals. Pin a corrected release and its checksums because language annotations and scene_info have been revised. name: RoboVQA
summary: RoboVQA pairs real office-task videos with language questions about progress, intermediate steps, and high-level planning. Its robot, human, and human-with-gripper embodiments support visual task reasoning across different ways of carrying out similar goals.
duration: Original long-horizon episodes have a reported mean of 102 seconds; segmented medium-horizon episodes have a reported mean of 14 seconds. Minimum and maximum durations are unknown for both units, and the dataset-wide range of VQA input-window lengths is unknown.
duration_short: Mean: full episode 102 s; medium-horizon segment 14 s; both min-max unknown
total: 238 hours of video reported by the paper/project; reused complete episodes, segments, and VQA pairs must not be added together.
tasks: Visual question answering about task progress
modalities: Real RGB video, task instructions, and multiround language questions and answers across embodiments; public continuous robot-control actions and complete environment-state vectors were not verified.
access: As of 2026-10-24: Open entry points: official Cloud Storage links and the official repository are public, with a Hugging Face mirror linked from the project. Coverage of original full videos and QA packages remains unverified. Dataset downloads and playback were not tested.
license: The official repository specifies Apache 2.0 for software and CC BY 4.0 for other materials. Mirrors do not alter original terms; package-specific attribution and additional conditions must be retained.

The 238-hour total does not reconcile directly with 5,246 * 102 seconds, so preserve the reported means instead of deriving a replacement. View-counting and reuse conventions remain unresolved. Published QA and intervention-rate experiments do not establish an interactive simulator, full control data, optimal counterfactual actions, or failure-cause labels.

name: MultiBypass140
summary: Clinical laparoscopic videos show Roux-en-Y gastric bypass operations from centers in Strasbourg and Bern. Hierarchical phase and step labels describe the surgical workflow, and a later annotation extension adds intraoperative adverse events and severity.
duration: Individual surgery range: 37-178 minutes, using global extrema across the three splits in Appendix Table 7. StrasBypass70 spans 41-178 minutes and BernBypass70 spans 37-145 minutes. The main text reports respective means of 110 and 72 minutes; the discussion instead reports 111 +/- 33 and 73 +/- 20 minutes (mean +/- standard deviation), retained as a reporting difference.
duration_short: Range 37-178 min; center means 110/72 min; also 111 +/- 33 / 73 +/- 20 min (mean +/- SD)
total: 140 surgeries, 70 per center. The reported 1 fps frame counts, 464,794 + 305,907 = 770,701, imply approximately 214.08 hours of temporal coverage; this is a derived total.
tasks: Intraoperative adverse-event detection and severity assessment
Future-step and event prediction from past context (derived)
modalities: Endoscopic RGB, temporal phase/step labels, and intraoperative adverse-event labels with severity.
access: Open download links, as checked on 2026-10-24: the official repository lists six data archives and annotation/visualization instructions. Actual downloads and per-file completeness were not tested.
license: The official README restricts code, models, and datasets to noncommercial scientific research under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Third-party code retains its own license.
family: MultiBypass140 combines StrasBypass70 and BernBypass70. The 2025 intraoperative adverse-event extension annotates the same surgeries rather than adding 140 new cases.
caveats: Standard deviations are not duration endpoints; the reported range comes from explicit split-level extrema. The differing center means are retained rather than silently reconciled. Sampling at 1 fps preserves the source surgery time scale. Labels cover 12 phases, 46 steps, and 5 adverse-event categories; severity is 1-5, with 0 indicating no adverse event. Adverse events do not automatically indicate operator misconduct, an omitted step, or complete protocol-compliance supervision. Positive-case counts and event-boundary coverage were not audited, and not every case can be assumed to contain an anomaly.

total: 220 source videos: 177 regular and 43 JIT. The paper reports 11,528 minutes, with that unit retained despite the unresolved conflict; trustworthy total hours are unknown. The 3,717 derived action clips are not 3,717 independent procedures.

name: MATT-Bench

duration: Per-clip minimum and maximum are unknown for the complete benchmark and each of its three subsets. The Ego4D-M temporal-attribution/point-of-no-return experiment reports a mean clip length of approximately eight seconds (240 frames at 30 fps), applicable only to that experimental scope. Independent mean or typical durations for EPIC-KITCHENS-M and HoloAssist-M are unknown.
duration_short: Ego4D-M temporal experiment mean ~8 s only; other subsets and overall duration unknown.
total: Unique video duration is unknown for MATT-Bench and each subset. The card lists Ego4D-M: 220,800 samples / 19,467 instructions; EPIC-KITCHENS-M: 299,715 / 12,283; HoloAssist-M: 562,209 / 1,786. These are not independent-video counts and must not be multiplied by eight seconds.
modalities: Real RGB action-attempt clips, instructions, semantic roles, and inherited Ego4D point-of-no-return and spatial-box annotations; XLSX and Parquet annotation releases.

license: The Hugging Face annotation card specifies CC BY 4.0; original videos retain upstream licenses.
family: Ego4D; EPIC-KITCHENS; HoloAssist: derived annotation extensions

Eight seconds must not be generalized to all MATT-Bench or to other subsets. Parent full-video duration is not benchmark input duration, and HoloAssist-M must not inherit HoloAssist statistics. MisEngine pairs real actions with different instructions to synthesize labels; human validity studies do not make these naturally occurring mistakes. Large combinatorial row counts are not counts of natural failures. Temporal and spatial supervision is inherited for Ego4D-M; the other parts provide semantic attribution only. An inherited point-of-no-return label is not automatically the irreversible point of an actual failure. Full-procedure omissions and recovery trajectories are not native supervision.

modalities: RGB and video features; original audio is not a consistent native benchmark input.
access: As of 2026-10-24: Public entry points: the author repository lists UNC Charlotte and Dropbox media links plus test temporal annotations. Linked package contents were not verified. Media downloads and complete package availability were not tested.
license: Dataset license not verified; code licenses do not establish rights to source surveillance videos.

caveats: Continuous surveillance context is not a multistep task-completion episode. Multiple-instance learning splits videos into instances as a training representation; instance lengths must not be conflated with original surveillance-video lengths. Native step, omission, correction, or optimal next-action annotations are absent, so performance does not establish long-horizon procedural state understanding.

duration_short: Main synthetic clips: fixed 5 s (design min=max); chunks 0.5 s
total: Main full set: 1,200 five-second clips, implying 6,000 seconds = 100 minutes, approximately 1.667 hours. It comprises 800 situational clips and 400 visual-channel clips arranged as 200 true/false-sign pairs; paired variants are not independent executions. modalities: Main set: synthetic egocentric robot chest-view video, textual signs, chunk-level labels, and explanations. Paper v2 also describes a separate real-video check.

family: Independent synthetic robot-view benchmark, with a separately described real-video sanity check in paper v2.
caveats: Use paper v2, available at the 2026-10-31 cutoff, to qualify the original v1 account. The canonical 5-second duration is the full clip; 0.5 seconds is a chunk. The verified 1,200-file manifest supersedes the earlier uncertainty about listed media, but it does not prove successful downloads or decoding. Short synthetic contexts do not establish long procedural dependencies or recovery planning. The HF history and raw-card endpoints returned HTTP 401 without authentication, which is an access limitation rather than evidence of missing data. Repository timestamps do not prove an exact first-public-release date.

caveats: The long-horizon characterization follows complete-recipe guidance and feedback structure, not proof that every video exceeds a duration threshold. Each row represents a video, not one feedback clip; message timestamps and the last feedback entry are not video endpoints. The main and advanced_planning configurations can reuse source videos and must not simply be added. Sampled output_actions fields were often empty, so do not assume one action per feedback message. Offline replay does not establish successful execution after a correction.

name: EgoServe / Vinci2
summary: EgoServe combines egocentric videos from EgoLife, HoloAssist, and CaptainCook4D with service-timing and response annotations. Semi-automatically generated and human-checked assistance supports evaluation of when to intervene and what guidance, reminders, or recovery advice to provide.
duration: Minimum and maximum durations are unknown for every source subset. HoloAssist subset mean approximately 4.59 minutes per video, derived as 14.6 hours * 60 / 191 videos; CaptainCook4D subset mean approximately 12.69 minutes, derived as 18.4 hours * 60 / 87 videos. EgoLife subset file/episode mean unknown; multiday history is not one video.
duration_short: Derived means: HoloAssist 4.59 min, CaptainCook4D 12.69 min; EgoLife unknown; min-max unknown
total: Source-specific video totals in Figure 2(c): EgoLife 95.3 hours, HoloAssist 14.6 hours, and CaptainCook4D 18.4 hours; summed total 128.3 hours.
modalities: Egocentric video and service text with human-checked assistance timing and content annotations.
access: As of 2026-10-24: The official project links the SitongGong/EgoServe Hugging Face release; parent videos must be obtained under each source dataset's access conditions. Dataset downloads and playback were not tested.
license: Licenses for the new annotations and all three parent datasets require separate checks; redistribution permission is unconfirmed.
family: EgoLife + HoloAssist + CaptainCook4D
caveats: Keep original videos, multiday memory histories, and model clip windows separate. Only HoloAssist and CaptainCook4D have matched video counts supporting derived means; do not construct a unified per-sample mean across all three sources. The Vinci2 paper, page 5 Figure 2(c) and section 3.2, reports 191 HoloAssist videos, 87 CaptainCook4D videos, and the first five days for three EgoLife participants; the plotted hours are subset totals. This mixes proactive assistance and everyday memory, not exclusively continuous manipulation. It is not an independent video collection, service appropriateness is not an industrial acceptance standard, and the unverified 547K-QA claim is not adopted.

name: CausalVQA
summary: Meta's CausalVQA asks about physical behavior and its consequences using selected video clips. Descriptive, counterfactual, hypothetical, anticipation, and planning questions support evaluation of causal reasoning and alternative-action outcomes.
duration: Final QA clips: reported mean 24.8 seconds and maximum 288.9 seconds; minimum unknown, so the complete minimum-maximum range is unknown. Parent-video duration range and mean are unknown.
duration_short: QA clips: mean 24.8 s, maximum 288.9 s; minimum unknown
total: The original selection pool contains 298 parent videos totaling about 12 hours. Deduplicated hours of final QA clips are unknown; the source-pool total is not the final clip total.
modalities: Video clips and questions/answers about descriptive, counterfactual, hypothetical, anticipation, and planning scenarios.
access: As of 2026-10-24: The official repository provides download instructions requiring an EgoExo license application; test answers are withheld. Dataset downloads and playback were not tested.
license: EgoExo License.
family: Ego4D / Ego-Exo licensing family
caveats: This record refers to Meta's 2025 CausalVQA. Longer parent recordings are cropped to the intervals needed for answers, yielding a mean of tens of seconds; a maximum near five minutes does not make the dataset uniformly long-horizon. Repeated questions and overlapping clips must not be added as independent video time. Paper v1 sections 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 describe the 12-hour source pool and cropping, and page 7 section 2.3.1 reports 24.8-second mean and 288.9-second maximum while noting that difficulty is not primarily long-video memory. A planning question category does not establish executable optimal-action labels.

name: EgoLife / EgoLifeQA
summary: EgoLife records six people sharing a home, including chores, collaboration, conversation, and social activity over a week. Transcripts, dense captions, and long-term questions support retrieval of objects and events and assistance that uses personal history.
duration: Individual released video files or shards: minimum, maximum, and mean unknown. Each participant has approximately 50 hours of ordered recording history spanning 7 days; this does not mean one continuous 50-hour video file.
duration_short: ~50 h of history/person over 7 days; individual file min-max and mean unknown
total: Approximately 50 hours per participant across 6 participants, yielding approximately 300 first-person hours (6 * approximately 50); simultaneous recordings from different participants are counted separately.
modalities: Egocentric and synchronized multiview video and audio; the project also describes gaze, IMU, and 3D data, with full release correspondence still requiring verification.
access: As of 2026-10-24: Official Hugging Face video resources are available at the documented entry point; the matching release coverage of all described modalities remains unverified. Dataset downloads and playback were not tested.
license: Hugging Face metadata specifies MIT while the project repository uses an S-Lab license. The scopes are inconsistent; check the agreement covering each specific file before fixing a release.
family: EgoLife
caveats: These are long everyday-life histories rather than a collection dedicated to continuous procedural tasks; household work, conversation, and social activity coexist. The project reports six participants, one week, and approximately 50 hours per person, without a released-shard duration range. Do not confuse searchable multiday history, individual file length, and synchronized-view totals, or assume uninterrupted overnight recording. Shared people and environments create identity/time leakage risks, and recording length is not the same as the evidence span required by a question.

summary: EgoMemReason adds cross-day questions and evidence annotations to existing EgoLife recordings. Entity, event, and behavior questions support reasoning about accumulated states, event order, and habits across multiple pieces of historical evidence.

name: HourVideo
summary: HourVideo evaluates reasoning over long egocentric videos selected from Ego4D. Questions cover summarization, recall, tracking, spatial and causal reasoning, counterfactuals, and navigation across everyday scenes.
duration: Selected videos range from 20 to 120 minutes, with a reported mean of approximately 45.7 minutes.
duration_short: Video range: 20-120 min; reported mean ~45.7 min
total: 500 selected videos totaling a reported 381 hours; this is not the total duration of Ego4D.
modalities: Video and language questions/answers; auxiliary captions are released separately.
access: As of 2026-10-24: Official repository, Hugging Face, and EvalAI entry points are documented; source videos follow Ego4D access conditions. Dataset downloads and playback were not tested.
license: The benchmark and development annotations must not enter training corpora, and the canary must be retained. Other redistribution permissions require checking the dataset card; source video follows Ego4D terms.
family: Ego4D
caveats: All selected videos are long, but the 77 everyday scene categories include both procedures such as cooking/cleaning and nonprocedural activity such as eating or watching television. Prediction tasks may truncate inputs at query timestamps; one-minute caption windows are not source-video durations. Paper section 2.3 reports the 20-120-minute range, approximately 45.7-minute mean, and 381-hour total; section 3.1 describes prediction-time truncation. Do not count Ego4D-derived footage again as new recordings. Navigation QA is not closed-loop navigation, and the benchmark should remain isolated from training under its stated restrictions.

name: LongVideoBench
summary: LongVideoBench pairs web videos with interleaved subtitles and multiple-choice questions requiring referring reasoning. Its mix of domains and duration groups supports evaluation of visual evidence retrieval and language understanding across different context lengths.
duration: Collection groups are 8-15 seconds, 15-60 seconds, 3-10 minutes, and 15-60 minutes. The design spans 8 seconds to 60 minutes, but exact observed minimum and maximum durations were not separately reported. Reported mean 473 seconds per video, equivalent to approximately 7.88 minutes.
duration_short: Design groups span 8 s-60 min; mean 473 s (~7.88 min); exact observed min-max unreported
total: Total hours unknown; the audited paper locations did not directly report a total. Do not multiply question counts by mean video duration.
modalities: Video, interleaved subtitles, and multiple-choice referring questions.
access: As of 2026-10-24: Official Hugging Face video/subtitle resources and a data loader are documented; the full release was not downloaded in the original check. Dataset downloads and playback were not tested.
license: The data license was not verified in the original source check.
family: Multi-domain web video
caveats: The four collection groups include many second-scale clips as well as minute-scale videos; movies, news, daily life, and knowledge content are not all procedural. Group boundaries do not establish that observed samples reach those exact endpoints. The introduction and section 3.1 define the groups, and Table 1 reports 3,763 videos with a 473-second mean. Interleaved subtitles and referenced evidence snippets are not complete-video durations. Subtitle access can bypass visual reasoning, so evaluate subtitle and video-only conditions separately.

name: OVBench / VideoChat-Online
summary: OVBench evaluates online understanding of past events, current observations, and future developments using multiple source datasets. Tasks include goal and step prediction, step verification, procedure recall, object localization, and motion prediction.
duration: Individual videos and evaluation prefixes: minimum, maximum, mean, and typical duration unknown.
duration_short: Video and evaluation-prefix duration distributions unknown
total: Deduplicated video hours unknown.
modalities: Video and image sequences with online task questions.
access: As of 2026-10-24: The official project provides a Hugging Face benchmark entry point and an evaluation repository. Dataset downloads and playback were not tested.
license: The data license was not verified in the original source check.
family: Multiple video and image-sequence sources
caveats: The official project describes six core task categories and sixteen subtasks spanning multiple sources; the proportion of short and long inputs is unknown. Past, present, and future are relative to a query, not evidence of a long full input. name: OVO-Bench
summary: OVO-Bench evaluates backward tracing, real-time perception, and forward active responding in streaming video. Source-video and prechunked releases support protocols in which a model recalls history, interprets current evidence, or waits until sufficient future evidence arrives.
duration: For the repository version checked in the audit, source-video and prechunked-video minimum, maximum, and mean durations are unknown. The reported 263.42 seconds is the mean query timestamp, not mean video duration or a uniform clip length.
duration_short: Video/clip durations unknown; 263.42 s is mean query timestamp, not video length
total: Deduplicated source-video hours unknown; the checked README reports 644 videos and 3,100 queries, which do not establish total hours.
modalities: Video and text queries, distributed as source videos and prechunked video packages.
access: As of 2026-10-24: The official Hugging Face source-video and prechunked-video releases have documented download instructions; the original check verified instructions only. Dataset downloads and playback were not tested.
license: Data: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, with inherited source-dataset terms. Code: MIT.
family: Multi-source online video
caveats: This mixes current perception, historical tracing, and waiting for future evidence; the actual short/long-video proportions are unknown. Keep src_videos separate from chunked_videos because chunks may reuse the same source prefix and cannot simply be summed. The checked README explicitly labels 263.42 seconds as Average query timestamp and provides separate source and chunk packages. The repository version differs from the early arXiv version, so pin the release. Forward responding evaluates response timing, not recommended robot or human actions.

name: STORM-Bench
summary: STORM-Bench tests reasoning from incomplete online evidence in real and simulated activities such as cooking, bicycle repair, health, music, and sports. Timestamped evidence, change-intensity labels, and Known/Uncertain judgments support state tracking and abstention when available observations are insufficient.
duration: Constructed compact episodes: minimum, maximum, mean, and typical duration unknown. Duration ranges and means of the upstream complete recordings are also unknown.
duration_short: Compact-episode and upstream full-recording durations unknown
total: Deduplicated hours of constructed episodes unknown; upstream dataset totals must not be transferred to this benchmark.
tasks: Online state tracking from video prefixes
modalities: Real and simulated video, questions/answers, temporal evidence, change-intensity annotations, and Known/Uncertain labels with reasons.
access: As of 2026-10-24: GitHub provides annotations, manifests, and evaluation code, while Hugging Face provides media for six subsets. Episode IDs differ between the two releases. Dataset downloads and playback were not tested.
license: A complete license was not verified; parent-data conditions require individual checks.
family: HD-EPIC + Ego-Exo4D + AI2-THOR + VirtualHome
caveats: Chronologically ordered real clips are assembled into compact episodes and are not necessarily temporally continuous in their original recordings; the benchmark also includes simulation rollouts. Distinguish concatenated playback duration from original elapsed time with omitted gaps, and do not present all constructed episodes as original long videos. The official README documents both this construction and differences in episode IDs and media layout between GitHub and Hugging Face releases. This benchmark is distinct from industrial STORM-PSR.

name: StreamingBench
summary: StreamingBench evaluates understanding and output timing across everyday and web video streams. Visual, audiovisual, sequential-question, and proactive-output settings support comparisons of real-time perception and use of preceding context.
duration: Complete videos: minimum, maximum, and mean unknown. The main evaluation uses the 60 seconds immediately preceding each query, a protocol window rather than a full-video range; the All Context setting uses a query-dependent prefix length.
duration_short: Full duration unknown; main context is 60 s before each query; All Context varies
total: Total hours for the 900 videos in the checked release are unknown; 4,500 QA items are not independent videos.
modalities: Video, audio, and text questions/answers.
access: As of 2026-10-24: Hugging Face resources and preprocessing scripts are documented; the full dataset was not downloaded in the original check. Dataset downloads and playback were not tested.
license: Repository code: MIT. Licenses for benchmark data and source videos were not confirmed in the original check.
family: Multi-source streaming video
caveats: The main window is the 60 seconds before the query, not the first 60 seconds of the video. Real-time, audiovisual, and long-context settings are mixed; they do not all measure long-term memory or procedural tasks. The checked README reports 900 videos and five query timestamps per video, and distinguishes Main context from All Context (+ Long Context). Pin the version for task counts; the unverified 5,134-QA count is not adopted.

name: Video-MME v1
summary: Video-MME v1 evaluates video understanding with human-written multiple-choice questions across six domains and thirty subdomains. Short, medium, and long groups enable comparisons across input lengths and video, audio, and subtitle conditions.
duration: Version 1 videos range from 11 seconds to 1 hour. Mean approximately 16.93 minutes, derived as 254 hours * 60 / 900 videos. Evaluation groups: short under 2 minutes, medium 4-15 minutes, and long 30-60 minutes.
duration_short: v1 range: 11 s-1 h; derived mean ~16.93 min
total: Version 1 contains 900 videos totaling 254 hours, as reported by the official project.
modalities: Video, audio, subtitles, and human-written multiple-choice questions.
access: As of 2026-10-24: The official project provides code and data entry points. Dataset downloads and playback were not tested.
license: Licenses for benchmark data and source videos were not verified in the original check.
family: General web video
caveats: The benchmark mixes short, medium, and long videos across domains; it is not uniformly long-horizon procedural content. This record and its duration statistics cover v1 only, not v2. The v1 introduction reports 11 seconds to 1 hour, 900 videos, and 254 hours; leaderboard groups define the three duration bands. Audio, subtitles, and multiple questions attached to one video do not add recording time. Global QA does not directly evaluate continuous procedural state tracking.

name: EgoStream (Forte, Lando, and Furnari)
summary: EgoStream evaluates episodic memory in streaming egocentric video across seven memory dimensions. Evidence moments and Answer Validity Windows support analysis of whether an incorrect answer reflects forgetting or a subsequent change in the world.
duration: Individual source videos, evaluation subclips, and input prefixes: minimum, maximum, and mean unknown. Recall-delay regimes extend from immediate recall to more than 8 hours, but this is memory delay, not a video-duration range.
duration_short: Video/subclip/prefix durations unknown; immediate to >8 h describes recall delay
total: Deduplicated source-video hours unknown; totals from the multiple parent datasets must not be imported as this benchmark's total.
modalities: Egocentric video and questions/answers, evidence moments, and Answer Validity Window annotations.
access: As of 2026-10-24: The original check verified the paper; availability of a complete usable dataset package and its license was not confirmed. Dataset downloads and playback were not tested.
license: Unverified. A Creative Commons license on the paper does not establish a data license.
family: Multiple egocentric QA source datasets
caveats: This is the EgoStream work by Forte, Lando, and Furnari; do not import statistics from namesakes or other Ego benchmarks. Not every question requires long memory, and the data are not a uniform collection of continuous procedural episodes. Record evidence moments, Answer Validity Windows, query delays, and input-video lengths separately. Paper section 3.1 draws from Ego4D, EgoLife, EgoTempo, Multi-Hop EgoQA, and HD-EPIC; appendix A.5 describes subclip cropping that preserves answer validity, and A.6 includes recall delays exceeding 28,800 seconds. Keep the watchlist status until release availability is confirmed.
